label: POST HOC - not pre-registered; descriptive only; specified 2026-11-15 after all camera-ready results were known

definitions.c_step: c_t = min(1, 1.0 / grad_norm_t), grad_norm_t = logged pre-clip total norm at optimizer step t
definitions.step_mapping: group generated at ledger generation_global_step s is weighted by c_{s+1}
definitions.bin_mass: S_b(T) = mean over directions A,B of the within-bin mean over panel questions of cumulative |A| (generation step < T); clip-weighted: |A| * c. Bins: frozen A40 cross-fit bins (analysis.json convention).
definitions.share_V1: S_b / total |A| (or |A|c) over all training groups before T  [analysis.json share_ratio convention]
definitions.share_V2: mean over directions of (sum of |A| over the bin's panel groups) / (sum over all panel groups); sums to 1 over the six bins
definitions.cbar_per_direction_mean: mean over directions of (sum |A|c / sum |A|) within the bin
definitions.frac_of_bin_raw_mass_per_direction_mean: mean over directions of (cell sum / bin sum)
definitions.step_type: each arm's own number of live groups in the step that generated the group
definitions.low_K_stratum: smallest positive K among the step's two groups; strata 1..15 within live count 1 or 2; all 3,736 steps of each run
definitions.flags: n<10, n<30 (n = contributing groups; for low_K, steps)

pooled_over_seeds.note: steps pooled across the three seeds (each run contributes its 3,736 steps)

ambiguities: Share denominator. V1 (shown in the note) divides the symmetric per-question bin mass by the arm's total over *all* training groups before T, as `analysis.json`'s `share_ratio` does; V2 uses the fraction of the *panel's* mass, averaged over directions (sums to 1 over the six bins). Largest |V2 − V1| in any share ratio: raw 0.212, clip-weighted 0.130. Both in the JSON.

Cross-fit averaging of derived ratios (c̄_b, fraction of bin mass). Pooled form = ratio of the two symmetric masses (shown; gives clip ratio = raw ratio × c̄^M/c̄^G exactly); alternative = mean over directions of the per-direction ratios. Largest difference: c̄ 0.089, fraction 0.373. Both in the JSON.
Cumulative vs interval mass. All T values are cumulative from step 0 (as in `analysis.json`); mass accrued only between evaluated steps is not computed.

Step type is arm-specific: the same question can sit in a 1-live step in one arm and a 2-live step in the other, so the M/G ratio within a type compares partly different question sets. A joint classification (by both arms' types, or by GRPO's type only) is not computed.
Clipped / not-clipped sub-split in section 2 was added so that the stated prediction (1-live and clipped steps) can be read; the request listed only the 1-vs-2 split.

Section 3 uses all 3,736 steps of each run (whole training set, no bins); restricting to steps that consumed a panel question would give far fewer steps. Pooling over seeds is done by pooling steps; per-seed tables are in the JSON.
Small-cell thresholds (10 and 30) are this note's choice; every cell reports its counts.

The pipeline's `c = min(1, 1/(g + 1e-6))` (the form torch's clip_grad_norm_ applies) differs from this note's c only at the 1e-6 level; the strict `> 1.0` rule excludes the steps whose logged norm is exactly 1.0 (count per run in `checks`). Logged norms are coarsely quantized (values such as 1.3515625).

grad_norm = 0 makes 1.0/grad_norm undefined. It occurs at exactly the steps with no live group (33–52 per run; checked both ways), which carry no mass; c is set to 1 there (the limit of min(1, 1/g), and the factor torch applies). It affects only the 'no live group' row of section 3, whose mean c is 1 by this rule.
